key_insight: The paper proposes coherent magnons as mediators of nuclear resonance energy transfer, aiming to bypass mass dilution and thermal spin cancellation that constrain phonon-based approaches.
engineering_relevance: If validated, this mechanism could shift metal-deuteride design constraints from lattice fracture limits toward controlled magnetic resonance and nuclear spin polarization.
method: Extend a generalized nuclear Dicke model to ferromagnetic-resonance magnons.
Model hyperfine-amplified M1 coupling and polarization-enabled relativistic M2 coupling.
Derive a Suhl-clamped scaling law for nuclear energy transfer.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical predictions of 14.2 MeV neutrons for Pd-106, 11.4 MeV neutrons for Ni-58, and 19.9 MeV alpha particles, but describes no experimental validation.
watch_item: Experimental feasibility remains unestablished, particularly whether sufficient coherent magnon excitation and nuclear spin polarization can coexist under realistic material conditions.
paper_title: Macroscopic Nuclear Resonance Energy Transfer Mediated by Coherent Magnons
